outcomes: A CI job that is not Putnami's uploads its change evidence document to Putnami Cloud with a workspace token, and the run shows its tests, coverage, components, changed-line coverage and dependency changes, marked as self-reported
nonGoals: Creating the observed workspace or its token: the runbook does it by hand for this slice
Uploading from a CI other than GitHub Actions or GitLab CI: Delivery has no provenance for it
Signing in as a person: the upload uses the workspace token alone

requirements.text: putnami cloud evidence-report --file <path> reads a protocol/evidence v1 document and opens its run with POST /v1/delivery/records under the PUTNAMI_CLOUD_TOKEN bearer: the subject's provider, numeric project id as repo, commit and branch, provenance gha or gitlab from the CI, the pull or merge request as changeRequest, conclusion failure when a test failed, else success, and a submission id derived from the CI job, so a repeated upload opens no second run.

The run carries under operational what the job tested, read with Git where the command was invoked: testedTree when the subject's commit is the merge the CI built (GitHub refs/pull/<n>/merge at GITHUB_SHA, a GitLab merged results or merge train pipeline at CI_COMMIT_SHA), else testedHeadTree; with it, baselineMergeBase of the document's base and commit. A value Git cannot compute is left out with a warning naming it and why. A run refused for its operational opens again without it.

After the run, it posts the tests and coverage of each component in one batch to POST /v1/delivery/records/reports, then the components, the changed-line coverage and the dependency changes, copied from the document, in a second batch under the same submission id. A batch with nothing to carry is not sent.

Each dependency change in the second batch keeps the before and after states the document gives it: the licenses and the known vulnerabilities, each with its id and severity, and an empty state as empty. A dependency change without a state uploads the same body as before the states existed. A batch refused with 413 for its size while it carries states is posted again without them, with a warning that names the refusal.

Without PUTNAMI_CLOUD_TOKEN, with a document that does not parse or validate, or with a generic CI, it sends nothing and exits non-zero with a message that names the cause. A refused run or batch exits non-zero with the route and the server's reason, and never prints the token; a run opened again without its operational counts as refused only when that call is refused too.
